bullets.text: A landslide, the Ashfell Slide, struck the Withel terraces and Cranmoor area of the Dreth mining region on 14 March 2026.
The slide damaged the lower road at Withel and prompted a warning for Withel terraces and Cranmoor in the early morning.
Human impact reported within the first four hours was limited to the evacuation of about 60 households from Withel terraces and of residents from Cranmoor.
The response in the window consisted of the warning and evacuation, and the cause of the slide had not been addressed in reports by the end of the window.
A warning is issued for Withel terraces and Cranmoor shortly after 07:20.
About 60 households are evacuated from Withel terraces and residents move out of Cranmoor as part of the evacuation.
Government sources report that the Ashfell slide has damaged the lower road at Withel.
The Ashfell slide damaged the lower road at Withel.
About 60 households were evacuated from Withel terraces, with residents also moved out of Cranmoor.
A warning was issued for Withel terraces and Cranmoor before residents were moved out.
